chunks: With this chain of narration, from Sayf ibn 'Umayra, from Mansur ibn Hazim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

One who passes a single day and prays five prayers in it, but does not recite 'Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad' in them, it will be said to him: 'O servant of Allah, you are not among those who pray (properly).'

key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah (Imam al-Sadiq, peace be upon him)
key_terms.سَيْفُ بْنُ عُمَيْرَةَ: Sayf ibn 'Umayra, a narrator in the chain
key_terms.قُلْ هُوَ اللَّهُ أَحَدٌ: Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad (Surah Al-Ikhlas), a chapter of the Quran
key_terms.مَنْصُورُ بْنُ حَازِمٍ: Mansur ibn Hazim, a narrator in the chain

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on reciting Surah Al-Ikhlas in daily prayers according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Thawab al-Amal*, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) underscores the spiritual weight of Surah Al-Ikhlas, equating its consistent recitation with the essence of Salah itself. The phrase 'you are not among those who pray' is interpreted by Shia scholars not as a negation of the prayer's validity, but as a critique of its spiritual incompleteness or a lack of true presence (khushu), highlighting the Surah's role as the core declaration of Tawhid. This reflects the broader Shia emphasis on the internal meaning of rituals, where reciting the chapter affirming God's unity is seen as the soul of the prayer.
